correctness.rationale: Vertex and edge mixed codes have explicit forms in a complete multipartite graph. Those forms prove that a complement has size at most two, identify the exact singleton and third-part collisions, and establish sufficiency of the remaining cases. Direct exhaustive verification checks every vertex and edge code on 128 multipartite types and 64,916 subsets through order ten.

evidence: Proposition 4.2 of the foundational work gives the valid complete-bipartite minimum formula.
Theorem 5 of the 2022 paper asserts N-1 when a part has size two and N-r otherwise for arbitrary complete multipartite graphs.
The corrected theorem agrees with the 2016 bipartite domain but disagrees with the broader 2022 statement for r>=3.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2022 statement would be broader coverage if correct, so it was tested at the statement level rather than dismissed by title. Its claimed generator sizes create unavoidable edge-edge or vertex-edge collisions; hence it does not validly imply the corrected theorem.

evidence: The original bipartite theorem gives N-1 when one part has size two and N-2 when both have size at least three.
The 2022 theorem claims N-r for K_{3,3,5}, namely 8.
The direct definition-level checker finds no mixed generator of size below 10 for K_{3,3,5}, while every one-vertex complement is valid because all three parts have size at least two.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The corrected theorem strictly preserves the valid prior bipartite implication while refuting the invalid multipartite extension. Because a false theorem cannot cover a correct claim by implication, the corrected classification remains original subject to the stated literature-search risk.

originality.rationale: The 2016 source correctly covers complete bipartite graphs. The 2022 source claims the arbitrary multipartite extension but its statement is contradicted by direct mixed codes for r>=3. No inspected source or targeted later search supplied the corrected all-set theorem. The new claim is therefore a correction plus a strictly stronger classification/enumerator, not a restatement of the covered bipartite case.
residual_risks: A later erratum, correction, thesis, or differently phrased non-indexed treatment may exist.
The finite exhaustive computation covers orders at most ten; the unrestricted claim relies on the symbolic proof.
